## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the best swell direction.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best wind direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the wave size this break works in.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> All 5 readable current sources were re-read and 4 new readable sources added: WSL 2022 Essentials, hawaii.surf, WannaSurf fields and Caldwell 2005 (JCR). WIND is now well supported from 4 readable publishers: Surf-Forecast (SE on the Pipeline listing, ESE on the Pipeline and Backdoor listing), WSL (calm or light SE), hawaii.surf (S-SE) and WannaSurf (S). All are within 45 deg of the profile's 135. SWELL DIRECTION: Surf-Forecast WNW/NW, WSL W-NW (Lopez: any NW, a slight west angle gives hollower waves), hawaii.surf 295-340 and WannaSurf NW-W all fit. Wikipedia instead says a W swell clears sand and a N swell then gives the best waves, so N (A-frame and Backdoor) is recorded as contradicting the 295-320 optimum. SIZE: hawaii.surf 6-15 ft faces, WSL a few feet overhead to triple overhead (about 8-18 ft, converted from overhead), WannaSurf from 3 ft, and Wikipedia up to about 20 ft. The profile's 4-15 is broadly right, but the top may be low. PERIOD: the first numeric support is hawaii.surf (16+ s for classic Pipe, 10-14 s favours Backdoor), a single community source. TIDE: Surf-Forecast (B&B listing) says all stages. hawaii.surf says it works most tides but is best on low-mid, recorded as a mild contradiction. SEASON: hawaii.surf Nov-Mar, Caldwell 2005 Oct-Mar high-surf season (region-wide, not spot-specific), Surf-Forecast summer-flat. REEF: Wikipedia, WannaSurf and hawaii.surf say flat lava/tabletop reef. The Surfertoday limestone claim (403, unchanged) remains a conflict. WannaSurf's own type field says 'Reef-coral' while its text says lava. Not readable (403): Surfertoday x2, SURFER, GoHawaii (reclassified official -> magazine per methodology v1.2; claims unchanged). The EOS Pipeline entry is paywalled. No Pipeline-specific peer-reviewed or measured bathymetry was found.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 3–5 ft | documented | S6 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | a few feet overhead to triple overhead · surfer heights (face) | documented | S9 | no separate setting; working range 4–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | no upper limit stated: First Reef faces run 6-15 ft on a solid winter swell, and Second Reef starts breaking outside from about 10-12 ft | documented | S1, S5, S6, S7, S10 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 1.0-1.5 m / 3-5 ft; the template does not say whether this is face or offshore swell height.
  - S6 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft”
- **Ideal range**: WSL says Pipe works best from a few feet overhead to triple overhead, a face height relative to the surfer (the evidence file's 8-18 ft is its own conversion).
  - S9 (World Surf League): “Pipe works best anywhere from a few feet overhead to triple overhead”
- **Maximum suitable**: hawaii.surf says First Reef faces run 6-15 ft on a solid winter swell, while Wikipedia, Surfertoday and SURFER (the last two search summaries) say Second Reef starts breaking at about 10-12 ft; WannaSurf's 4m+ / 12 ft bracket is open-ended; no source gives a size at which Pipe stops working.
  - S10 (hawaii.surf): “Wave faces on First Reef run from six to fifteen feet on a solid winter swell.”
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “As the size at Pipe increases, over 12 feet usually, Second Reef on the outside”
  - S5 (Surfertoday): “It is only activated when the surf hits 10 or 12 feet.”
  - S7 (SURFER): “Surfer's Pipeline profile also notes that the second reef begins to break once the swell hits 10 feet.”
  - S6 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft”

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |

Notes:

- **Break type**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break with lefts and rights, WannaSurf a hollow, fast left, and WSL names Backdoor as the shallower right.
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Pipeline in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has pretty consitent surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat.”
  - S3 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Reef breaks provide lefts and rights.”
  - S6 (WannaSurf): “DirectionLeft...PowerHollow, Fast, Powerful”
  - S9 (World Surf League): “There's also Backdoor, a right-hander that is shallower, gnarlier and more prone to closing out.”
- **Orientation**: No excerpt gives the reef orientation; Surfertoday (search summary) only says the left tube runs eastward.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it an exposed reef break.
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Pipeline in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has pretty consitent surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat.”
- **Bathymetry**: WannaSurf and hawaii.surf describe a flat lava reef, but Surfertoday (search summary) says First Reef is limestone covered by carbonate rock, not lava; the sources agree on a flat, shallow tabletop reef (6-10 ft deep per Surfertoday, 2-3 ft of water at times per a Surf-Forecast user review, a few feet per GoHawaii), three reefs that break with increasing size, and sand build-up causing close-outs.
  - S6 (WannaSurf): “The left tube at Pipeline relies on a west-angled swell, which refracts onto a shallow flat lava reef about 80 yards offshore.”
  - S10 (hawaii.surf): “The wave breaks roughly sixty to eighty yards offshore over a flat lava reef that rises suddenly from deeper water”
  - S4 (Surfertoday): “The First Reef is a 15,000-year-old limestone plateau broken up by a few narrow crevasses, covered by carbonate rock (not lava), black basaltic rock, coral, and turf algae”
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “The reef at Pipe is a flat tabletop reef, with several caverns on the inside”
  - S4 (Surfertoday): “The waves at Pipeline start to break over a local shallow tabletop reef that rests between six and 10 feet deep.”
  - S8 (GoHawaii.com (Hawaii tourism site)): “The break is known for powerful waves that break over a sharp reef no more than a few feet from the surface.”
  - S2 (Surf-Forecast.com): “At times, there is literally only 2 to 3 feet of water over the reef”
  - S6 (WannaSurf): “Pipeline is actually a series of reefs (3) which allows it to work on a variety of swell sizes”
  - S4 (Surfertoday): “The Pipeline surf zone comprises three reef structures that produce rideable waves as the swell increases - the farther out to sea, the deeper the water.”
  - S1 (Wikipedia): “When sand accumulates on the reef at Pipeline, the waves can become unpredictable and violently”
  - S6 (WannaSurf): “If sand is built up on the northern edge of the reef, murderous closeouts occur on a regular basis.”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell direction · ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives WNW (Pipeline listing) and NW (Banzai/Backdoor listing), WSL and WannaSurf a west-angled swell, SURFER (search summary) W to NW and hawaii.surf WNW to NW (295-340), whereas Wikipedia says a strong north swell gives the best waves once a west swell has cleared the sand.
- **Wind · offshore**: Surf-Forecast's Pipeline listing and WSL give southeast, Surf-Forecast's Banzai/Backdoor listing east-southeast, hawaii.surf south or southeast and WannaSurf south.
- **Tide · preferred stage**: Surf-Forecast's Banzai/Backdoor listing says good surf at all stages of the tide, while hawaii.surf says it works across most stages but low to mid tide (roughly -1 to +1 ft) gives maximum hollowness.
- **Geography · bathymetry**: WannaSurf and hawaii.surf describe a flat lava reef, but Surfertoday (search summary) says First Reef is limestone covered by carbonate rock, not lava; the sources agree on a flat, shallow tabletop reef (6-10 ft deep per Surfertoday, 2-3 ft of water at times per a Surf-Forecast user review, a few feet per GoHawaii), three reefs that break with increasing size, and sand build-up causing close-outs.
